snippet.title: What Did Pompeii Look Like? Pompeii's Last Day Visualized | (Ai Reconstruction)
snippet.description:
Step into Pompeii on October 24, 79 AD—hours before Mount Vesuvius erupted and buried the city under 20 feet of ash.

Using AI reconstruction and archaeological evidence, we've brought ancient Pompeii back to life. Watch the Forum bustling with 15,000 Romans. See the amphitheater—the oldest stone amphitheater in the world. Walk through the Forum Baths with their advanced hypocaust heating system. Experience the streets, the markets, the temples—all frozen in time by the catastrophic eruption.

This isn't the ruins you see today. This is Pompeii as it actually was—a thriving Roman city at the peak of its power, minutes before disaster struck.

🏛️ IN THIS VIDEO:
- The Forum - Political and religious center of Pompeii
- Temple of Jupiter - Massive columns and sacred architecture  
- Forum Baths - Roman engineering masterpiece with heated floors
- House of the Faun - 3,000 square meter elite villa with stunning mosaics
- The Amphitheater - 20,000 seat arena, oldest surviving in Rome
- Daily life - Markets, bakeries, and the reality of slavery in ancient Rome
- The Eruption - How Vesuvius destroyed everything in 24 hours

📚 HISTORICAL FACTS:
- Population: 11,000-15,000 people
- Date: October 24, 79 AD (new evidence suggests this date, not August 24)
- Eruption power: 100,000 times the atomic bombs of Hiroshima/Nagasaki
- Buried under: 4-6 meters (13-20 feet) of volcanic ash and pumice
- Death toll: Estimated 13,000-16,000 people
- Rediscovered: 1748, after being lost for 1,700 years

This reconstruction is based on decades of archaeological excavations, ancient texts from Pliny the Younger (the only eyewitness account), and cutting-edge AI technology to visualize what the ruins looked like when they were whole.

snippet.title: What Maya Cities Really Looked Like at Their Peak (AI Reconstruction)
snippet.description:
What did the Maya world look like before the jungle took it back? Forget the gray stone ruins—this was a civilization of vibrant blood-reds, blinding white stucco, and cities that scraped the sky. 🏛️✨

In this documentary, we use AI reconstruction to peel back the emerald canopy and travel 1,500 years into the past. Following the latest archaeological data and LiDAR scans, we’ve rebuilt the Maya world at its absolute zenith. Witness the "Stone Mountains" of the rainforest and the bustling streets of a society that mastered time and the stars long before the arrival of Europe.

🎬 In this journey, we explore:
The Red Superpower: Step into the Great Plaza of Tikal, a metropolis of 100,000 people painted in brilliant cinnabar.

Masterpieces of Engineering: How the Maya terraformed the jungle to build massive reservoirs and "white roads" (Sacbeob).

The Monster Portals: Experience the terrifying "Chenes" architecture—doorways designed to swallow you into the underworld.

Acoustic Magic: The secret science behind the "chirping" pyramids of Chichén Itzá.

The High-Stakes Game: The brutal reality of Pok-a-Tok, where sport and ritual sacrifice collided.

The Collapse: What really happens when a civilization pushes its environment to the breaking point?

snippet.title: What Did  Troy Look Like In 1200 BC (AI Reconstruction)
snippet.description:
Step into Troy in 1200 BC—the legendary Bronze Age fortress city before the Trojan War, before it fell, when its massive walls stood at full height and 10,000 people called it home.

For 3,000 years, people thought Troy was just a myth from Homer's Iliad. Then in 1870, Heinrich Schliemann discovered the real city buried in Turkey. Using archaeological evidence, ancient texts, and AI reconstruction, we've brought Troy back to life—not as ruins, but as it actually looked at the peak of its power.

This is Troy VI, the fortress that controlled the Dardanelles strait and dominated trade between Europe and Asia.

🏛️ IN THIS VIDEO:
- The Citadel Walls - 9 meters (30 feet) high limestone and mudbrick fortifications
- The Sawtooth Pattern - Unique defensive design found nowhere else in the Bronze Age
- The South Gate - Wide enough for two chariots, flanked by massive sacred stone pillars
- Megaron Houses - Elite residences on terraced levels rising to the royal palace
- The Lower Town - 30 hectares (75 acres) protected by a massive wooden palisade
- Trade Networks - Goods from Afghanistan, India, Egypt, and Greece
- The Trojan Plain - Famous horse breeding grounds and farmland
- The Destruction - Earthquake in 1300 BC, fire in 1180 BC

📚 HISTORICAL FACTS:
- Location: Hisarlik, northwestern Turkey (8km from Dardanelles strait)
- Period: Troy VI (1700-1300 BC) - Late Bronze Age peak
- Citadel area: Hilltop fortress on strategic height
- Lower town: 30 hectares - much larger than originally thought
- Population: Estimated 5,000-10,000 people (citadel + lower town + plain)
- Wall height: 9 meters (30 feet) - limestone base + mudbrick superstructure
- Wall thickness: Over 4 meters at the base
- Gates: 5 different gates, each uniquely designed
- Trade goods: Lapis lazuli (Afghanistan), carnelian (India), amber (Baltic), Mycenaean pottery
- Discovered: 1870 by Heinrich Schliemann
- UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1998

⚔️ THE TROJAN WAR:
While we can't prove Homer's Trojan War happened exactly as described in the Iliad, archaeological evidence shows Troy VIIa (1300-1180 BC) was violently destroyed by fire around 1180 BC. Bodies were found in the rubble. This matches the timeframe of the legendary war, making Troy one of the most fascinating intersections of myth and history.

⏱️ TIMESTAMPS:
0:00 - Introduction: From Myth to Reality
0:30 - The Citadel: Walls, Towers & Strategic Location
2:00 - The Gates: South Gate & Sacred Pillars
3:00 - Inside the Citadel: Terraces, Houses & Palace
4:00 - The Lower Town: Workshops, Trade & Daily Life
5:30 - The Trojan Plain: Farms, Horses & Agriculture
6:00 - Destruction: Earthquake 1300 BC, Fire 1180 BC
7:00 - Closing: Legend Meets Reality

🎯 WHY TROY MATTERS:
Troy's location at the Dardanelles—the narrow strait connecting the Aegean Sea to the Black Sea—made it one of the most strategically important cities in the ancient world. Control this strait, and you control trade between two continents. This is why Troy was wealthy, powerful, and worth fighting over.


📖 SOURCES & RESEARCH:
- Archaeological excavations by Heinrich Schliemann (1870-1890)
- University of Cincinnati excavations (1988-present)
- University of Tübingen research (1988-present)
- "Troy and Homer: Towards a Solution of an Old Mystery" by Joachim Latacz
- UNESCO World Heritage Site documentation
- Homer's Iliad (8th century BC) - literary source
- Hittite texts mentioning Wilusa (believed to be Troy)

🏺 ARCHAEOLOGICAL EVIDENCE:
The ruins of Troy show multiple layers of cities built on top of each other over 4,000 years. Troy VI (1700-1300 BC) was the largest and most impressive, with massive fortification walls and evidence of extensive trade networks. The unique sawtooth wall pattern, rectangular towers, and overlapping gate defenses show sophisticated military architecture. The lower town discovery in the 1990s revealed Troy was far larger than previously thought—not just a small citadel but a major Bronze Age city.

snippet.description:
The city of #Ur was one of the most important #Sumerian city-states in ancient #Mesopotamia during the 3rd millennium BC, and one of the best-preserved and most spectacular remains of this ancient city is the Great #Ziggurat of Ur.

The Great Ziggurat, which is today located in the Dhi Qar Province in southern Iraq is a massive step pyramid construction measuring 64 metres in length, 46 metres in width and 30 metres in height. This height, however, is just speculation, as only the bottom of the structure survives today and even this has been heavily renovated.

snippet.title: What Medieval London Really Looked Like (AI Reconstruction)

snippet.title: Virtual tour in ancient Athens (5th century BC) - 3D reconstruction
snippet.description:
3D reconstruction of Classical Athens in the late 5th century BC.  The city is presented the way it would look in the years before the defeat in the Peloponnesian War (404 BC).
The city of Athens was completely destroyed by the Persian army in the years 480-479 BC. In the years that followed, the Athenians managed to rebuild their city and by the middle of the 5th century BC, the statesman and general Pericles ordered an extensive construction programme that made Athens the centre of classical Greece. It was the time when the great temples on the Acropolis hill were built (Parthenon, Erechtheion) and many buildings of public administration for the Athenian Democracy.

The video presents almost all of the important monuments, spaces and areas within the city. The 3d reconstructions were made after the most recently published international research and a great effort was made to be as accurate as possible. Of course simplifications and artistic license are present in order to technically manage a big project as this one.
